one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with an elegiac tribute to Senate President Jovito R. Salonga -- his mentor, benefactor, guru, friend, and surrogate father -- recalling Salonga's foremost teaching that one must prioritize values money cannot buy (integrity, honor, dignity, patriotism, love for God) over the things money can buy. He then pivots to commentary on Grace Poe's 9-6 Supreme Court victory of March 8, 2016, contrasting the 'hubris' of critics who denounced the decision before its release as a 'culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust' with the 'humility' of Poe's pre-verdict statement that she would accept whatever the Court decided. Using his signature mirror-construction aphorism ('If that is not hubris, I do not know what is' / 'If that is not humility, I do not know what is'), he then offers six 'sidelights' on the case: the Court was not remiss given the Poe case's greater complexity than FPJ's; the original ponente in both Poe and FPJ cases was overruled by the majority; both Poes won by an identical three-vote margin (9-6 vs 8-5); the rumor of a P-Noy 'secret candidate' is refuted by the split among his six appointees (four with the majority, two -- including close friend Justice Reyes -- with the minority); he ascribes the vote pattern to judicial independence, noting justices know they will be 'judged by history, not by baseless knee-jerk reactions'; and asks whether Poe will vindicate her adoptive father by winning the Comelec count and congressional canvass -- 'Abangan!' He closes with a civic-cultural appreciation of three classical music events: the Rotary Club of Makati's 50th-anniversary Vienna Spring Concert (where club president Eddie Yap announced the first air-quality monitoring station in Makati, funded by P50,000 contributions from CJ and 120 members totaling P6 million); the Johann Strauss Society's gala concert; and his own son Dr. Jose Artemio C. Panganiban III's Brahms performances at the CCP and BDO Center. He concludes by urging sponsors to reach not just the mature and privileged but also millennials and the general public, convinced Filipinos appreciate the classics as much as pop music.
